title: Shopify or WooCommerce?

rows: Monthly fee, zero server headaches
Fastest to launch and easiest to run
Best when you sell products and want it simple
Apps cost extra as you grow
Your own hosting, one-time build cost
Fully flexible, any feature possible
Best for big catalogues and custom flows
Needs updates and a bit of care

foot: I run one store on each. Ask me which fits you.
li:
Shopify or WooCommerce? I get this question every week, and I run one store on each, so here is the honest answer.

Shopify
→ Monthly fee, zero server headaches
→ Fastest to launch, easiest for staff to run
→ Best when you sell products and want it simple
→ Apps add cost as you grow

WooCommerce
→ Your own hosting, one-time build cost
→ Fully flexible, any feature is possible
→ Best for big catalogues and custom order flows
→ Needs updates and a bit of care

MYNAH MART runs on Shopify. Royal User UK runs on WooCommerce. Both take Cash on Delivery orders every day.

The platform matters less than two things: does it load fast on a phone, and can the owner manage it without calling a developer?

Planning a store? Tell me what you sell and I'll tell you which one I'd pick for you.

#Shopify #WooCommerce #Ecommerce #SmallBusiness #WebDevelopment

title: I built my own e-commerce brand.
li:
I don't just build stores for clients. I run one myself.

MYNAH MART is my own multi-category store in Bangladesh, built on Shopify. Running it every day taught me more than any tutorial:

→ Many customers still want to order on WhatsApp, even with a cart right there
→ Cash on Delivery orders need a fast confirmation step or they get cancelled
→ Most visitors arrive from a Facebook ad on a phone with weak data, so every second of loading costs money
→ Combo and bundle offers quietly raise the average order
→ If the owner can't update stock and prices alone, the store stalls

That is the lens I bring to every client website: not 'does it look nice', but 'will it take orders tomorrow morning, and can you run it yourself?'

If you're planning a store, I'm happy to share what has worked for mine.

foot: Built for clinics, diagnostic centres and dental practices in Dhaka.
li:
What a clinic website actually needs (and what it doesn't).

I looked at a lot of clinic and diagnostic-centre websites in Dhaka this week. Most of them are a brochure. A patient needs something simpler:

1. Book an appointment in 3 taps: name, phone, time. Not a 12-field form.
2. Doctors with photos and schedules. People choose a doctor, not a building.
3. Click-to-call and WhatsApp on every page. Most patients still want to talk first.
4. Location, hours and parking where you can see them.
5. Fast on a phone. A worried parent on 4G will not wait 8 seconds.
6. Google Business Profile with reviews, because that's where the search starts.

None of this is expensive. It is just deciding that the website's job is to get a patient through the door.

If you run a clinic, diagnostic centre or dental practice and your site doesn't do these six things, I'm happy to show you a sample homepage that does.

title: 4 ways to cut Cash-on-Delivery cancellations
rows: Confirm within the hour
A quick call or WhatsApp while the intent is fresh.
Show the delivery charge before checkout
Surprise fees are the #1 reason people refuse at the door.
Give a delivery window, then keep it
'Tomorrow 2–6 pm' beats '3–5 working days'.
Send a tracking update
One message when it ships. Fewer 'where is my order' calls, fewer refusals.
foot: Learned the hard way at MYNAH MART.
li:
Cash on Delivery is how Bangladesh buys online. It is also where stores quietly lose money: the parcel comes back, and you've paid the courier twice.

Four things that cut cancellations at my own store, MYNAH MART:

1. Confirm within the hour. A quick call or WhatsApp while the intent is fresh.
2. Show the delivery charge before checkout. Surprise fees are the number one reason people refuse at the door.
3. Give a delivery window and keep it. 'Tomorrow 2–6 pm' beats '3–5 working days'.
4. Send one tracking update when it ships. Fewer 'where is my order?' calls, fewer refusals.

None of these are design features. They are workflow features, and a good store build makes them automatic: delivery charge calculated by zone, confirmation message triggered on order, status updates sent without anyone typing.

This is the part of e-commerce most developers never see, because they don't run a store. I do, so I build it in.

#Ecommerce #CashOnDelivery #Bangladesh #Shopify #WooCommerce
fb:
COD order বাতিল কমানোর ৪টা উপায় (নিজের store থেকে শেখা) 📦

Bangladesh-এ online কেনাকাটার বেশিরভাগই Cash on Delivery। আর এখানেই store চুপচাপ টাকা হারায়: parcel ফেরত আসে, courier-কে দুইবার টাকা দিতে হয়।

MYNAH MART-এ যা কাজে লেগেছে:
1️⃣ এক ঘণ্টার মধ্যে confirm: ছোট একটা call বা WhatsApp
2️⃣ checkout-এর আগেই delivery charge দেখানো, দরজায় surprise fee-ই refuse-এর ১ নম্বর কারণ
3️⃣ delivery-র সময় বলা আর সেটা রাখা: 'কাল ২–৬টা' > '৩–৫ কর্মদিবস'
4️⃣ ship হলে একটা tracking message

এগুলো design না, workflow। ভালো store build-এ এগুলো automatic হয়: zone অনুযায়ী delivery charge, order হলেই confirmation message, status update নিজে থেকে।

title: 5 questions to ask before you hire a web developer
rows: Can I see something live, not just screenshots?
Open it on your phone and try to order.
Who owns the domain, hosting and admin?
You should. Always.
What happens after launch?
Support period, update cost, response time.
Is the price fixed, and what does it include?
Pages, products, payments, training. In writing.
Can I run it without you?
If the answer is no, keep looking.
foot: Ask me these. I like answering them.
li:
5 questions to ask before you hire a web developer (including me).

1. Can I see something live, not just screenshots? Open it on your phone and try to place an order.
2. Who owns the domain, hosting and admin login? You should. Always. I've seen businesses lose their own website because it was registered in a developer's name.
3. What happens after launch? Support period, cost of updates, how fast they reply.
4. Is the price fixed, and what exactly does it include? Pages, products, payments, training. Get it in writing.
5. Can I run it without you? If the answer is no, keep looking.

A good developer is happy to answer all five. If someone gets uncomfortable, that tells you something.

My answers, for the record: mynahmart.com and royaluseruk.com are live and take orders daily; everything is registered in the client's name; 30 days of support after launch; fixed price in writing before we start; and I walk you through the admin so you don't need me for a price change.

title: The cheapest sales fix on any website:
sub: Most customers in Bangladesh want to ask one question before they buy. If the only option is a contact form, they leave. One green button on every page keeps the conversation, and the sale, alive.
foot: Takes 20 minutes to add. Ask me how.
li:
The cheapest sales fix I know for any website in Bangladesh: a WhatsApp button.

Most customers here want to ask one question before they buy. 'Is this in stock?' 'Can you deliver to Uttara tomorrow?' 'Is the price for one or two?'

If the only option is a contact form, they leave. If there is a green WhatsApp button on every page, the conversation starts, and most of the time, the order follows.

At Royal User UK, WhatsApp ordering sits right next to the cart, and plenty of customers use it. At MYNAH MART the same. It is not a sign the website failed. It is how people here like to buy.

Two details that matter:
→ Pre-fill the message with the product name, so the customer doesn't have to type
→ Reply fast. A WhatsApp lead that waits an hour is usually gone

It takes about 20 minutes to add properly. If your site doesn't have one, that's the first thing I'd fix.

#Ecommerce #WhatsApp #Bangladesh #SmallBusiness #WebDesign
fb:
যেকোনো website-এর সবচেয়ে সস্তা sales fix: একটা WhatsApp button। 💬

Bangladesh-এ বেশিরভাগ customer কেনার আগে একটা প্রশ্ন করতে চান। 'stock-এ আছে?' 'কাল Uttara-য় delivery হবে?' 'দামটা একটার না দুইটার?'

শুধু contact form থাকলে তারা চলে যায়। প্রতিটা page-এ সবুজ WhatsApp button থাকলে কথা শুরু হয়, আর বেশিরভাগ সময় order-ও হয়।

Royal User UK আর MYNAH MART দুই জায়গাতেই cart-এর পাশে WhatsApp order আছে, আর অনেকে সেটাই ব্যবহার করেন। এটা website-এর ব্যর্থতা না, এখানকার মানুষ এভাবেই কিনতে পছন্দ করেন।

২টা জিনিস খেয়াল রাখবেন:
✔️ message-এ product-এর নাম আগে থেকে লেখা থাকুক

pill: Why I build the way I do
title: When your own money is on the line, you learn fast what a website is for.
sub: I've built websites since 2022. In 2026 I launched my own store, MYNAH MART. Nothing teaches you faster than watching real orders come in, and real customers drop off, on a site you built.
foot: Mahi Uddin Ahmed · Website & E-commerce Developer, Dhaka
li:
When your own money is on the line, you learn fast what a website is actually for.

I've been building websites since 2022. In 2026 I launched my own store, MYNAH MART. Nothing taught me faster than watching real orders come in, and real customers drop off, on a site I built myself.

Things I used to think mattered: the hero animation, the perfect font pairing, a long About page.

Things that actually moved the numbers: a 3-second load on a cheap phone, the delivery charge shown before checkout, a WhatsApp button, a COD confirmation that goes out in minutes, and an admin simple enough that I could update 40 prices on a Friday night without touching code.

That's why every client site I build now starts from the owner's side of the counter, not the developer's. The question is never 'does it look good?' It's 'will it take orders tomorrow morning, and can you run it without me?'

If you're a founder planning a store or a business website, I'd be glad to talk.

#Entrepreneurship #Ecommerce #WebDevelopment #Bangladesh #Shopify

title: If your site takes longer than 3 seconds on a phone,
big: half your visitors are already gone.
sub: Most of your customers are on a mid-range phone, on 4G, coming from a Facebook ad. They did not come to wait. Compress the images, cut the apps you don't use, lazy-load below the fold, and test on a real phone, not your laptop.
foot: Want a free speed check of your site? Send me the link.
li:
If your website takes longer than 3 seconds to load on a phone, about half of your visitors are already gone.

That is not a design opinion. It is what happens to ad traffic: someone taps a Facebook ad on a mid-range phone on 4G, the page spins, they go back to scrolling. You paid for that click.

The usual causes I find on business and store websites:
→ Product photos uploaded straight from the camera, 3–5 MB each
→ Apps and plugins installed once and never removed, each loading its own scripts
→ A slider with six giant images above the fold
→ No lazy-loading, so the whole page loads before anything shows
→ Tested only on the developer's laptop on office Wi-Fi

The fixes are not glamorous: compress and resize images, remove dead apps, defer non-critical scripts, lazy-load below the fold, and test on a real phone.

At MYNAH MART this is a monthly check, because most of our visitors arrive from ads on phones.

Want a free speed check of your site? Send me the link and I'll tell you what's slowing it down.
